You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>
## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

use core::marker;

/// Generic peripheral accessor
pub struct Periph<PER: PeripheralSpec> {
    _marker: marker::PhantomData<PER>,
}

/// Peripheral data
pub trait PeripheralSpec {
    /// RegisterBlock associated with peripheral
    type RB;
    /// Address of the register block
    const ADDRESS: usize;
    /// Debug name
    const NAME: &'static str;
}

unsafe impl<PER: PeripheralSpec> Send for Periph<PER> {}

impl<PER: PeripheralSpec> core::fmt::Debug for Periph<PER> {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut core::fmt::Formatter) -> core::fmt::Result {
        f.debug_struct(PER::NAME).finish()
    }
}

impl<PER: PeripheralSpec> Periph<PER> {
    ///Pointer to the register block
    pub const PTR: *const PER::RB = PER::ADDRESS as *const _;

    ///Return the pointer to the register block
    #[inline(always)]
    pub const fn ptr() -> *const PER::RB {
        Self::PTR
    }

    /// Steal an instance of this peripheral
    ///
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// Ensure that the new instance of the peripheral cannot be used in a way
    /// that may race with any existing instances, for example by only
    /// accessing read-only or write-only registers, or by consuming the
    /// original peripheral and using critical sections to coordinate
    /// access between multiple new instances.
    ///
    /// Additionally, other software such as HALs may rely on only one
    /// peripheral instance existing to ensure memory safety; ensure
    /// no stolen instances are passed to such software.
    pub unsafe fn steal() -> Self {
        Self {
            _marker: marker::PhantomData,
        }
    }
}

impl<PER: PeripheralSpec> core::ops::Deref for Periph<PER> {
    type Target = PER::RB;

    #[inline(always)]
    fn deref(&self) -> &Self::Target {
        unsafe { &*Self::PTR }
    }
}

/// Raw register type (`u8`, `u16`, `u32`, ...)
pub trait RawReg:
    Copy
    + From<bool>
    + core::ops::BitOr<Output = Self>
    + core::ops::BitAnd<Output = Self>
    + core::ops::BitOrAssign
    + core::ops::BitAndAssign
    + core::ops::Not<Output = Self>
    + core::ops::Shl<u8, Output = Self>
{
    /// Mask for bits of width `WI`
    fn mask<const WI: u8>() -> Self;
    /// `0`
    const ZERO: Self;
    /// `1`
    const ONE: Self;
}

macro_rules! raw_reg {
    ($U:ty, $size:literal, $mask:ident) => {
        impl RawReg for $U {
            #[inline(always)]
            fn mask<const WI: u8>() -> Self {
                $mask::<WI>()
            }
            const ZERO: Self = 0;
            const ONE: Self = 1;
        }
        const fn $mask<const WI: u8>() -> $U {
            <$U>::MAX >> ($size - WI)
        }
        impl FieldSpec for $U {
            type Ux = $U;
        }
    };

Generate Rust register maps from SVD files.

This repository provides a tool that converts ARM CMSIS-SVD descriptions into source files that represent hardware peripheral registers and fields. The tool accepts an SVD file as input and produces register maps suitable for use in device support code.

Usage

  svd2rust [OPTIONS] <input.svd>

See the project documentation or the generated help output for available options and examples.

# ============ Case conversion and sanitization ============
RUST_KEYWORDS = set(["as","break","const","continue","crate","else","enum","extern","false","fn","for","if","impl","in","let","loop","match","mod","move","mut","pub","ref","return","self","Self","static","struct","super","trait","true","type","unsafe","use","where","while","async","await","dyn","abstract","become","box","do","final","macro","override","priv","typeof","unsized","virtual","yield","try"])

def to_snake_case(s):
    import re
    # Remove %s placeholder first? Caller should handle, but also handle here
    s = s.replace("%s", "").replace("%S", "")
    # Replace - and space and / etc with _
    s = re.sub(r'[^A-Za-z0-9_]', '_', s)
    # Split by _
    parts = s.split("_")
    out_parts = []
    for p in parts:
        if p == "":
            continue
        # If part is all upper (with digits) -> lower
        # Check if part has at least one letter and all letters are upper
        has_lower = any(c.islower() for c in p)
        has_upper = any(c.isupper() for c in p)
        if not has_lower and has_upper:
            # all upper
            out_parts.append(p.lower())
        elif not has_lower and not has_upper:
            # digits only
            out_parts.append(p)
        else:
            # mixed: camel to snake
            # Insert _ before Upper following lower/digit, and before Upper followed by lower when preceded by Upper? e.g., "FooBar" -> "Foo_Bar" -> "foo_bar", "FOOBar" -> "FOO_Bar"?
            t = re.sub(r'(?<=[a-z0-9])(?=[A-Z])', '_', p)
            t = re.sub(r'(?<=[A-Z])(?=[A-Z][a-z])', '_', t)
            # Now split t by _ and lower each?
            for sub in t.split("_"):
                if sub == "":
                    continue
                out_parts.append(sub.lower())
    res = "_".join(out_parts)
    res = re.sub(r'__+', '_', res)
    return res

def to_pascal_case(s):
    import re
    s = s.replace("%s", "").replace("%S", "")
    s = re.sub(r'[^A-Za-z0-9_]', '_', s)
    parts = s.split("_")
    out = ""
    for p in parts:
        if p == "":
            continue
        # p may be like "FOO", "Bar", "foo", "123", "TIMER0"
        # For each, first char upper, rest lower (but preserve digits)
        # If p is all digits? Keep as is
        if p.isdigit():
            out += p
        else:
            # Find leading digits? e.g., "123PER" -> "123per"? Our earlier logic: p[0].upper + rest lower
            # For "123PER": p[0]='1', upper='1', rest='23PER' lower='23per' => '123per'
            # For "FOO": 'F' + 'oo' => 'Foo'
            # For "Bar": 'B' + 'ar' => 'Bar'
            # For "foo": 'F' + 'oo' => 'Foo'
            out += p[0].upper() + p[1:].lower() if len(p) > 1 else p.upper()
    return out

    return to_snake_case(s).upper()

    if case is None or case == "" or case == "unchanged":
        # unchanged: keep as is? But need to remove %s? And replace invalid chars? For interrupt (unchanged), keep original case, but still need to sanitize? Interrupt names like GPIOA_IRQ stay as is.
        # Remove %s?
        import re
        t = s.replace("%s", "").replace("%S", "")
        # Replace invalid chars with _? For unchanged, keep case, but replace - etc with _?
        t = re.sub(r'[^A-Za-z0-9_]', '_', t)
        return t
    elif case == "snake" or case == "s":
        return to_snake_case(s)
    elif case == "pascal" or case == "p":
        return to_pascal_case(s)
    elif case == "constant" or case == "c":
        return to_constant_case(s)
    else:

    # If starts with digit, prefix _

    # If keyword, suffix _

    # If contains invalid chars? Already handled, but ensure starts with _ or letter?
    # Also handle "_" alone? Keep.
    # Replace any remaining invalid? Should already be valid.
    import re
    s = re.sub(r'[^A-Za-z0-9_]', '_', s)
    if s[0].isdigit():

def parse_int(s):
    if s is None:
        return None
    s = s.strip()
    if s == "":

    # Remove underscores? SVD may have 0x4000_0000? Unlikely in SVD, but handle.
    s = s.replace("_", "")
    try:
        if s.lower().startswith("0x"):

        elif s.lower().startswith("0b"):
            return int(s, 2)
        elif s.lower().startswith("#"):
            # binary? e.g., #1? Unlikely. Treat as?
            return int(s[1:], 2) if set(s[1:]) <= set("01") else int(s[1:])
        else:
            # decimal, may be like "0"? Handle?
            # Could be like "0x1234"? Already handled.
            # Could be like "1234"? decimal.
            # Could be like "true"/"false" for bools? Not int.
            return int(s, 0)

    value = parse_int(val_text) if val_text is not None else None
    is_default = (is_default_text is not None and is_default_text.strip().lower() == "true")
    return {"name": name, "description": desc, "value": value, "isDefault": is_default}

def parse_enumerated_values(evs_elem):
    if evs_elem is None:

# ============ SVD parsing helpers ============
def parse_int(s):
    if s is None:
        return None
    s = s.strip()
    if s == "":
        return None
    # Handle hex with 0x, also with #? SVD uses 0x... or decimal, also may have 0b? Handle.
    # Remove underscores? SVD may have 0x4000_0000? Unlikely in SVD, but handle.
    s = s.replace("_", "")
    try:
        if s.lower().startswith("0x"):
            return int(s, 16)
        elif s.lower().startswith("0b"):
            return int(s, 2)
        elif s.lower().startswith("#"):
            # binary? e.g., #1? Unlikely. Treat as?
            return int(s[1:], 2) if set(s[1:]) <= set("01") else int(s[1:])
        else:
            # decimal, may be like "0"? Handle?
            # Could be like "0x1234"? Already handled.
            # Could be like "1234"? decimal.
            # Could be like "true"/"false" for bools? Not int.
            return int(s, 0)
    except:
        # Try decimal?
        try:
            return int(s)
        except:
            return None

def get_child_text(elem, tag, default=None):
    if elem is None:
        return default
    c = elem.find(tag)
    if c is not None and c.text is not None:
        return c.text.strip()
    return default

def get_child_int(elem, tag, default=None):
    t = get_child_text(elem, tag, None)
    if t is None:
        return default
    v = parse_int(t)
    return v if v is not None else default

# Data classes as dicts
def parse_enumerated_value(ev_elem):
    name = get_child_text(ev_elem, "name", "")
    desc = get_child_text(ev_elem, "description", "")
    val_text = get_child_text(ev_elem, "value", None)
    is_default_text = get_child_text(ev_elem, "isDefault", None)
    value = parse_int(val_text) if val_text is not None else None
    is_default = (is_default_text is not None and is_default_text.strip().lower() == "true")
    return {"name": name, "description": desc, "value": value, "isDefault": is_default}

def parse_enumerated_values(evs_elem):
    if evs_elem is None:
        return None
    name = get_child_text(evs_elem, "name", None)
    usage = get_child_text(evs_elem, "usage", None)
    derived = evs_elem.get("derivedFrom", None)
    vals = []
    for ev in evs_elem.findall("enumeratedValue"):
        vals.append(parse_enumerated_value(ev))
    return {"name": name, "usage": usage, "derivedFrom": derived, "values": vals}

def parse_field(field_elem, reg_access=None, reg_size=None):
    name = get_child_text(field_elem, "name", "")
    desc = get_child_text(field_elem, "description", "")
    # bit info: bitOffset/bitWidth, bitRange, lsb/msb
    bit_offset = get_child_int(field_elem, "bitOffset", None)
    bit_width = get_child_int(field_elem, "bitWidth", None)
    bit_range = get_child_text(field_elem, "bitRange", None)
    lsb = get_child_int(field_elem, "lsb", None)
    msb = get_child_int(field_elem, "msb", None)
    offset = None
    width = None
    if bit_offset is not None and bit_width is not None:
        offset = bit_offset
        width = bit_width
    elif bit_range is not None:
        # format [msb:lsb] e.g., [7:0]
        m = re.match(r'\s*\[\s*(\d+)\s*:\s*(\d+)\s*\]', bit_range)
        if m:
            a = int(m.group(1)); b = int(m.group(2))
            offset = min(a,b)
            width = abs(a-b)+1
    elif lsb is not None and msb is not None:
        offset = lsb
        width = msb - lsb + 1
    elif bit_offset is not None:
        # width 1? Or need bitWidth? If only offset, assume width 1? Actually SVD requires width, but handle.
        offset = bit_offset
        width = 1
    else:
        offset = 0
        width = 1
    access = get_child_text(field_elem, "access", reg_access)
    # Normalize access: read-only, write-only, read-write, writeOnce, read-writeOnce? Map to r/w/rw?
    # enumeratedValues: may have multiple? Usually one. Handle first? Actually field may have <enumeratedValues> directly (one) - but spec allows multiple with usage? We'll take all and merge? For simplicity, take first that matches usage? Original handles usage read/write.
    evs_list = []
    for evs in field_elem.findall("enumeratedValues"):
        evs_list.append(parse_enumerated_values(evs))
    # dim for field? Handle?
    dim = get_child_int(field_elem, "dim", None)
    dim_incr = get_child_int(field_elem, "dimIncrement", None)
    dim_index = get_child_text(field_elem, "dimIndex", None)
    derived = field_elem.get("derivedFrom", None)
    return {"name": name, "description": desc, "offset": offset, "width": width, "access": access, "enumeratedValues": evs_list, "dim": dim, "dimIncrement": dim_incr, "dimIndex": dim_index, "derivedFrom": derived, "elem": field_elem}

def parse_register(reg_elem, dev_size=None, dev_access=None, dev_reset=None, dev_reset_mask=None):
    name = get_child_text(reg_elem, "name", "")
    desc = get_child_text(reg_elem, "description", "")
    addr_offset = get_child_int(reg_elem, "addressOffset", 0)
    size = get_child_int(reg_elem, "size", dev_size)
    access = get_child_text(reg_elem, "access", dev_access)
    reset_val_text = get_child_text(reg_elem, "resetValue", None)
    reset_val = parse_int(reset_val_text) if reset_val_text is not None else dev_reset
    # resetMask?
    reset_mask_text = get_child_text(reg_elem, "resetMask", None)
    reset_mask = parse_int(reset_mask_text) if reset_mask_text is not None else dev_reset_mask
    # fields
    fields = []
    fields_elem = reg_elem.find("fields")
    if fields_elem is not None:
        for f in fields_elem.findall("field"):
            # field access defaults to register access? Handled in parse_field via reg_access
            fields.append(parse_field(f, reg_access=access, reg_size=size))
    # dim
    dim = get_child_int(reg_elem, "dim", None)
    dim_incr = get_child_int(reg_elem, "dimIncrement", None)
    dim_index = get_child_text(reg_elem, "dimIndex", None)
    alt_group = get_child_text(reg_elem, "alternateGroup", None)
    # alternateRegister? Handle as alternateGroup? SVD has alternateRegister for alternate? Ignore.
    derived = reg_elem.get("derivedFrom", None)
    # writeConstraint, etc. ignore for now
    return {"name": name, "description": desc, "addressOffset": addr_offset, "size": size, "access": access, "resetValue": reset_val, "resetMask": reset_mask, "fields": fields, "dim": dim, "dimIncrement": dim_incr, "dimIndex": dim_index, "alternateGroup": alt_group, "derivedFrom": derived, "elem": reg_elem, "type": "register"}

def parse_cluster(cluster_elem, dev_size=None, dev_access=None, dev_reset=None):
    name = get_child_text(cluster_elem, "name", "")
    desc = get_child_text(cluster_elem, "description", "")
    addr_offset = get_child_int(cluster_elem, "addressOffset", 0)
    # clusters may have size? Ignore
    dim = get_child_int(cluster_elem, "dim", None)
    dim_incr = get_child_int(cluster_elem, "dimIncrement", None)
    dim_index = get_child_text(cluster_elem, "dimIndex", None)
    alt_group = get_child_text(cluster_elem, "alternateGroup", None)
    derived = cluster_elem.get("derivedFrom", None)
    # registers inside cluster: direct <register> and <cluster> children (no <registers> wrapper? Actually our test showed direct, but also handle <registers> wrapper for robustness)
    children = []
    # Check for <registers> wrapper inside cluster? In our first cluster test, we had <registers> wrapper which was ignored (empty). So handle both.
    regs_wrapper = cluster_elem.find("registers")
    if regs_wrapper is not None:
        for child in regs_wrapper:
            if child.tag == "register":
                children.append(parse_register(child, dev_size, dev_access, dev_reset))
            elif child.tag == "cluster":
                children.append(parse_cluster(child, dev_size, dev_access, dev_reset))

    for child in cluster_elem:
        if child.tag == "register":
            # Avoid double if already handled via wrapper? If wrapper exists, direct also? In our first test, wrapper had registers but direct had none? Actually first test had <cluster><name>...</><registers><register>... - so wrapper path handled. Direct path would also find? No, direct children are <name>,<description>,<addressOffset>,<registers> - not <register>, so no double.
            # But to avoid double when both? Check if child is inside wrapper? No, direct loop only looks at immediate children that are register/cluster, not inside wrapper. So safe.
            children.append(parse_register(child, dev_size, dev_access, dev_reset))
        elif child.tag == "cluster":
            children.append(parse_cluster(child, dev_size, dev_access, dev_reset))
    return {"name": name, "description": desc, "addressOffset": addr_offset, "dim": dim, "dimIncrement": dim_incr, "dimIndex": dim_index, "alternateGroup": alt_group, "derivedFrom": derived, "children": children, "elem": cluster_elem, "type": "cluster"}

def parse_peripheral(periph_elem, dev_size=None, dev_access=None, dev_reset=None, dev_reset_mask=None):

    # size/access/reset at peripheral level? Inherit from device? Actually peripheral may have size/access/resetValue?
    p_size = get_child_int(periph_elem, "size", dev_size)
    p_access = get_child_text(periph_elem, "access", dev_access)
    p_reset_text = get_child_text(periph_elem, "resetValue", None)
    p_reset = parse_int(p_reset_text) if p_reset_text is not None else dev_reset
    p_reset_mask_text = get_child_text(periph_elem, "resetMask", None)
    p_reset_mask = parse_int(p_reset_mask_text) if p_reset_mask_text is not None else dev_reset_mask
    return {"name": name, "description": desc, "groupName": group, "baseAddress": base, "items": items, "interrupts": interrupts, "dim": dim, "dimIncrement": dim_incr, "dimIndex": dim_index, "derivedFrom": derived, "size": p_size, "access": p_access, "resetValue": p_reset, "resetMask": p_reset_mask, "elem": periph_elem}

def parse_device(root):
    # root is <device>
    name = get_child_text(root, "name", "UNKNOWN")
    desc = get_child_text(root, "description", "")
    address_unit = get_child_int(root, "addressUnitBits", 8)
    width = get_child_int(root, "width", 32)
    size = get_child_int(root, "size", width)
    access = get_child_text(root, "access", "read-write")
    reset_text = get_child_text(root, "resetValue", None)
    reset_val = parse_int(reset_text) if reset_text is not None else 0
    reset_mask_text = get_child_text(root, "resetMask", None)
    reset_mask = parse_int(reset_mask_text) if reset_mask_text is not None else None
    # cpu
    cpu_elem = root.find("cpu")
    cpu = {}
    nvic_prio = None
    if cpu_elem is not None:
        nvic_prio = get_child_int(cpu_elem, "nvicPrioBits", None)
        cpu = {"nvicPrioBits": nvic_prio}
    else:
        cpu = {"nvicPrioBits": None}
    # peripherals
    periph_elem = root.find("peripherals")
    periphs = []
    if periph_elem is not None:
        for p in periph_elem.findall("peripheral"):
            periphs.append(parse_peripheral(p, dev_size=size, dev_access=access, dev_reset=reset_val, dev_reset_mask=reset_mask))
    return {"name": name, "description": desc, "addressUnitBits": address_unit, "width": width, "size": size, "access": access, "resetValue": reset_val, "resetMask": reset_mask, "cpu": cpu, "nvicPrioBits": nvic_prio, "peripherals": periphs, "elem": root}

    reset_mask_text = get_child_text(root, "resetMask", None)

    /// Modifies the contents of the register by reading and then writing it.
    ///
    /// E.g. to do a read-modify-write sequence to change parts of a register:
    /// ```ignore
    /// periph.reg.modify(|r, w| unsafe { w.bits(
    ///    r.bits() | 3
    /// ) });
    /// ```
    /// or
    /// ```ignore
    /// periph.reg.modify(|_, w| w
    ///     .field1().bits(newfield1bits)
    ///     .field2().set_bit()
    ///     .field3().variant(VARIANT)
    /// );
    /// ```
    /// or an alternative way of saying the same:
    /// ```ignore
    /// periph.reg.modify(|_, w| {
    ///     w.field1().bits(newfield1bits);
    ///     w.field2().set_bit();
    ///     w.field3().variant(VARIANT)
    /// });
    /// ```
    /// Other fields will have the value they had before the call to `modify`.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn modify<F>(&self, f: F) -> REG::Ux
    where
        for<'w> F: FnOnce(&R<REG>, &'w mut W<REG>) -> &'w mut W<REG>,
    {
        let bits = self.register.get();
        let value = f(
            &R {
                bits,
                _reg: marker::PhantomData,
            },
            &mut W {
                bits: bits & !REG::ONE_TO_MODIFY_FIELDS_BITMAP | REG::ZERO_TO_MODIFY_FIELDS_BITMAP,
                _reg: marker::PhantomData,
            },
        )
        .bits;
        self.register.set(value);
        value
    }
